data.title: Hess Midstream upgraded at Raymond James as Chevron restructuring selloff overdone
data.description:
Hess Midstream (HESM) rose 2.2% in Friday's trading as Raymond James raised its rating to Market Outperform from Market Perform with a $32 price target, saying its recent selloff following the Chevron (CVX) restructuring has created an attractive entry point for investors.

The Bakken contract reset was severe, reducing estimated 2027 EBITDA by $400M while pausing distribution growth and increasing leverage, yet Chevron's (CVX) ~38% ownership cancellation, contribution of D-J Basin assets, and contract extensions to 2045 provide Hess Midstream (HESM) with a meaningful exchange of value for the lower rates, Raymond James analyst J.R. Weston said.

The pause in 2027 distribution growth has weighted on Hess Midstream (HESM) sentiment, but the payout looks supported by $525M-$625M of guided adjusted free cash flow against $420M-$425M of distribution, which Weston said should allow leverage to move from 3.75x-4x to the 3.5x-3.75x longer-term target through 2029.

While fixed reservation payments expire after 2029, the analyst expects the existing payout to remain covered via retained free cash flow, modest D-J growth, and potential operating efficiencies.

"All in, risk is overstated and growth upside is feasible (though not necessary)," Weston wrote.

data.title: OpenAI says it will train frontier models models in closed system with no internet access
data.description:
OpenAI (OPENAI) said on Friday that it is going to train its frontier artificial intelligence in a more secure environment, putting them in a closed system with no internet access.

“Working closely with cloud providers, we’ve added new controls throughout our infrastructure, reduced the attack surface that agents can exploit, and improved our methods for detecting misaligned behavior and attempts to cross security boundaries,” OpenAI said in a statement. “These protections overlap, so that containment can hold even if an individual control fails—a strategy known as defense in depth.”

The changes come after the Hugging Face incident in July as well as other instances in which AI models acted in ways other than intended. 

Led by CEO Sam Altman, OpenAI added that the investments have allowed the company to detect and stop misaligned behavior before damage was caused. The company cited an example on Sept. 20 in which an internal research model exploited a misconfiguration in a DNS resolver to gain limited access. The incident was contained, and the weakness indicated that further work was needed.

Nonetheless, OpenAI added that “increasingly capable models can find vulnerabilities or misconfigurations in even the most secure systems,” and it's up to companies like OpenAI, Anthropic (ANTHRO), and others to fix them. 

“These red-teaming experiments discovered previously unknown software vulnerabilities, as well as misconfigurations in our research infrastructure. We’ve remediated weaknesses our red-teaming agents discovered and—where these issues were present in open-source software—have worked with the relevant maintainers, under our Patch the Planet initiative, to disclose and fix them,” OpenAI explained.

The company continued: “As our red-teaming experiments continued, the number of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations that our agents identified declined significantly. While we view this as an encouraging signal about the strength of our infrastructure, we expect that future models will be able to identify and exploit vulnerabilities of which we’re not yet aware. We therefore view continuous red-teaming as a core part of our long-term strategy for strengthening the security of our research environments.”

Reinforcement learning training and internal inference of OpenAI's frontier models resumed on Oct. 1.

data.title: S&P 500 eyes third straight quarter of 25%+ earnings growth
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) is on track for another period of robust profit expansion in the third quarter of 2026, even as higher oil and gas prices raise cost pressures across the economy.

FactSet data show the index’s blended year-over-year earnings growth rate at 29.5%. If that figure holds once all companies report, it would mark the third consecutive quarter of earnings growth above 25% for the benchmark.

Profitability remains exceptionally strong. The blended net profit margin for the S&P 500 stands at 14.9%. Should this rate become the final result, it would represent the second-highest net profit margin recorded since FactSet began tracking the metric in 2009.

Reporting is still early, with only 24% of S&P 500 companies having released results so far. Among those that have reported, 83% delivered earnings per share above analysts’ estimates, while 66% posted positive revenue surprises.

The combination of elevated growth and resilient margins suggests large-cap companies continue to convert sales into profits at a high rate despite commodity-price headwinds. As more results arrive in the coming weeks, investors will watch whether the current blended figures hold or shift as the remaining three-quarters of the index reports.

S&P 500 Funds: (SPY), (VOO), (IVV), (RSP), (SSO), (UPRO), (SH), (SDS), (SPXU), (FXAIX), (VFIAX), (VFFSX), and (SWPPX).

data.title: Genmab rises, Corcept falls on late-stage antibody-conjugate data for ovarian cancer
data.description:
• Genmab (GMAB) is up ~10% in Friday trading after reporting that a phase 3 trial of its antibody-drug conjugate, rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S), met its primary goal for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
  • In the intent-to-treat population, Rina-S, a folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeted, topoisomerase I (TOPO1)-inhibitor ADC, led to a 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death compared to investigator's choice of chemotherapy. In the primary analysis set group, the figure was 67%.
  • A secondary endpoint, overall survival, was also met in both populations. 
  • No new safety concerns were found in the RAINFOL-02 trial.
  • Corcept Therapeutics (CORT), which markets Lifyorli (relacorilant) for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, is down ~21% on the news.

data.title: Anthropic unifies Claude Chat and Cowork for enterprise plans
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) has unified Claude Chat and Cowork for enterprise plan subscribers that can be used on web, desktop and mobile devices.

"The new unified Claude experience brings chat and Cowork together on web, desktop, and mobile," Anthropic posted today on its Claude Support webpage. "Members no longer choose between chat and Cowork before they start. Every conversation starts as a chat, and when a task needs to run code or work with files, Claude continues the same conversation in an isolated cloud sandbox managed by Anthropic, then returns the finished work for review."

The new unified experience was made generally available today but currently requires an administrator to turn it on. Anthropic said the unified experience will be turned on by default beginning Nov. 16.

Iovance sees long-term response for Amtagvi in first-line melanoma
data.description:
• An analysis of phase 2 data found that a one-time treatment of Iovance Biotherapeutics' (IOVA) Amtagvi (lifileucel) combined with Merck's (MRK) Keytruda (pembrolizumab) led to a 62.5% objective response rate and a 29.2% complete response rate after a median follow-up of 50.9 months as a frontline treatment for advanced melanoma.
  • Median overall survival, however, was not reached at the timepoint.
  • The analysis of the IOV-COM-202 trial also found that median progression-free survival was 19.8 months and the disease control rate was 83.3%.
  • Amtagvi, a polyclonal tumor infiltrating lymphocyte ("TIL") cellular immunotherapy, was granted accelerated approval in 2024 for individuals with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who failed on a PD-1 inhibitor.
  • Iovance has also started enrollment in TILVANCE-301, a phase 3 study examining Amtagvi in combination with Keytruda compared with Keytruda alone in patients with untreated, unresectable, or metastatic melanoma.
